correctness.rationale: Uniform fixed-weight words correspond bijectively to weak zero-gap compositions; a one-zero deletion lowers a unique positive gap, so distinct positive gaps are precisely the output coupons. Conditional inclusion-exclusion gives the finite formula. Dirichlet-multinomial uniformity gives the limiting tail; a reciprocal-Beta estimate and a harmonic marginal sum prove the mean, including the constant. Independent literal deletion/source enumeration (702 words) and 75 exact tail checks passed; these experiments are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The actual observation model has unequal output probabilities set by random zero-run lengths; mere deletion-sphere size misses the sampling-time behavior. The theorem identifies a mathematically nontrivial lack of uniform integrability: a proper finite-valued limiting read-count law has infinite expectation even though each finite source ensemble has logarithmic mean with an explicit constant. The exact finite formula applies to all marker counts, not only a contrived small case; scope is naturally motivated by repeated readout of sparse binary sequences.
